title: Artlist Pricing 2026: What Every Plan Costs
summary: Artlist pricing structures determine which platforms and commercial projects are legally cleared for your video content.
body_markdown:
## Artlist pricing plans and license coverage


### The Social Creator plan for individual platforms


When a creator tries to use the same license to cover multiple YouTube channels or a secondary Instagram handle, they hit the Social plan's one-account-per-platform limit. This plan is strictly for personal content.


Consequently, any video produced for a paying client or a third-party brand violates the license. Because Artlist ties coverage to specific linked URLs, any content posted to an unlinked account will trigger automated copyright claims that demonetize the video immediately.


### The clearlist mechanism for automated protection


To manage these permissions, Artlist utilizes a Clearlist (sometimes referred to as a Whitelist) which serves as the digital bridge between a user’s subscription and the social media platforms.


By adding a specific channel URL to the Clearlist in the account settings, the creator notifies Artlist’s automated Content ID system that the channel is authorized to host their assets.


If a video is uploaded to a channel not present on this list, the platform’s scanners flag the music as unlicensed. For Social plan users, this list is limited to one entry per platform, meaning the protection is hard-coded to a single digital identity.


### Music & SFX vs. Music & SFX Pro limits


Access to the library is provided by the standard Music & SFX plan, but the scope of the license is limited to personal projects only.


Moving to the Pro version is the required step for commercial work, as it's the entry-level tier that includes "Client Work" rights. Without the Pro designation, a freelance editor cannot legally hand over a finished file to a business.


The business would lack the sub-license necessary to broadcast or host the media on their own corporate sites.


### Artlist Max: The all-in-one creative bundle


By combining music, sound effects, footage, and templates into a single subscription, Artlist Max reduces the friction of managing multiple line-item licenses.


This bundle supports high-output creators who need a unified legal umbrella for diverse asset types across various media formats.


The run is the meter, not the steps inside it, so studios use[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) to automate asset handoffs because a complex ten-step filing sequence costs exactly one credit, just like a simple two-step move.


This ensures that breaking work into granular, reliable steps (the foundation of professional automation) never results in a higher bill, as seen on their published pricing page where every flow run is a single credit regardless of its internal complexity.


The following table outlines the current cost structures and the specific AI and client permissions attached to each tier.

The need for multi-user seats or increased legal indemnity typically triggers the jump from Max to Enterprise.


### Enterprise solutions for large-scale teams


Only the Enterprise tier offers customized legal terms and indemnification for teams exceeding a specific headcount or budget threshold. It removes the standard seat limits that prevent a large agency from sharing a single login.


This policy ensures that every editor is covered under a centralized corporate policy. Because this tier has the highest allocation of AI credits, large teams can generate specialized assets without hitting the monthly caps that stall production in lower-tier plans.
